I am very disappointed with this steamer; design is poor-- it has too many parts – 2.5 stars. I am a steamer fanatic who mostly cooks everything with steam; this is my 15th steamer! Unfortunately, this is not even worth the money I have to lay out for this, in my opinion.

I have been steaming most of my meals for about 30 years. In those 30 years, I owned or previously owned 14 steamers. This is my 15th steamer and it is a whopping disappointment. I put this through the paces and it is one of my least favorite steamers. Yes it works, but it is cumbersome and bulky and has too many moving parts.

WHAT is in the BOX - In addition to the instruction manual, this comes in 11 parts as follows:

- Base unit
- Heater cap (also known as steam guard)
- Three (3) steam tray bottoms
- Three (3) steaming basket "rims" (upper, middle, and lower or what I call small, medium, and large)
- Top lid
- Rice bowl
- Drip Tray

FEATURES
- The steaming controls are LED and it comes with preset times for eggs, rice, fish, chicken/meat, and vegetables. I do not need this but newbies might like it.

- There is a keep-warm function (it is unclear for how long) and a timer function that allows steaming to be delayed anywhere from 1 minute to 12 hours and 59 minutes. I tested both the timer and keep-warm feature and they work well.

- The baskets are an opaque plastic and each basket is two loose pieces.

- The steamer has boil-dry protection so that it turns off if the reservoir is out of water.

LIKES
- The steamer cooks almost equally with all three baskets simultaneously. I usually put the food that gets done the quickest (the most delicate foods like fish) on top away from the intensity of the steam. The uppermost basket does not cook as fast but this is expected.

- It can steam a lot of food since it has three vertical levels.

- I can steam 18 eggs at one time--six in each basket. When I steam eggs, I want them to steam the same. I tested this and the eggs steamed in the top basket were less cooked than those in the bottom basket. However, this is to be expected. Note that I leave the uncooked eggs on the counter for about one hour before steaming so that they do not break during cooking.

- The keep-warm and delay-start features are nice to have.

- When in operation, the steamer is relatively quiet until the food is ready; that is when the beeps sound.

- A full reservoir provides enough steam for at least 60 minutes of steaming which is very generous; most steamers only last 45 minutes on full.

- Descaling is easy just like it is for all the other steamers I own. This steamer will develop mineral build up on the heating element. All that has to be done is to fill the reservoir with equal parts vinegar and water and heat on high for twenty minutes. I actually use almost 100% vinegar in most of my steamers. I have not used this long enough yet to implement descaling.

DISLIKES
- The opaqueness of the baskets makes it difficult to see how the food is doing during steaming.

- Each basket comes in two pieces. It is also easy to have the bottom slip out if not seated correctly. In addition, the top has to be placed on the uppermost basket just right or that will slip off too.

- The LED is awkward in the sense that the on/off button has to be pressed more than once to start the steaming process. I kept thinking the steaming would start and then the unit would turn off. The only way I could tell I got it right was when the two dots (:) blinked.

- There are way too many moving parts. The design of the baskets is very poor. They come apart like a springform pan without the spring.

- The unit with the baskets is also big and bulky and does not collapse into a small enough footprint for storage.

- There is no reservoir refill hole on the outside of the steamer. If I were serial steaming various foods, I would run out of water and would have to handle a hot steamer to refill or wait until it cools. When there is an outside hole for the reservoir, I can use a teapot or something with a spout to refill the steamer during operation or between operations without getting burned. Since the reservoir holds about 60 minutes of water, this issue will not affect me much as I rarely do more than two steaming sessions that go beyond one hour.

- Although this does not affect me at all, beware that the steamer is tall when in use. In addition, the cord is short as is expected of any appliance such as this.

In summary, I am utterly disappointed in this steamer. Although it works, it is cumbersome to use, too bulky, and has too many pieces. The design is not well-thought out. My main disappointment is that each basket is two pieces (a flat removable bottom and a plastic ring for the sided), which makes absolutely no sense to me.

For those who are interested, here are MY STEAMERS - PAST and PRESENT

PAST 3 STEAMERS that eventually broke:

- One small round Black and Decker Steamer (extinct now) which was great and super small but only lasted about two years. This was my first steamer that I purchased in the 1990's.

- One [[ASIN:B00004SPEI Krups Optisteam Plus]]. I had this since February 1999 and it was my most used steamer and very similar to the Oster steamer.

- One [[ASIN:B00073HLMU Oster 5711 Mechanical Food Steamer]], which I used daily for my oatmeal and most dinners until it died.

CURRENT 12 STEAMERS (counts one that I have three of):

- This one [[ASIN:B07ZFKMVL3 AmazonBasics 12.5 Quart 3-Tiered Digital Food Steamer]]. The basket design is poor and it is too bulky. I would pass.

- This [[ASIN:B07H79RGVJ Secura Electric Food Steamer]]. This is my favorite steamer. No plastic comes in contact with the food. It has few moving parts and steams evenly and well. If I had the room, I would buy a second one because, as of this writing, I cannot bear the thought of being without it.

- One [[ASIN:B01MZF7ZFZ Breville Steam Zone steamer]] – this one is large; has an annoying ticking noise during operation and cooks unevenly. The option of using only the steaming tray w/o the pots allows for cooking large items like fillets of fish. I rarely use this steamer due to its lackluster functionality.

- One [[ASIN:B008FX6KH6 T-fal VC133851 Balanced Living Compact Electric Food Steamer, 4-Quart, Silver]] – this one is too small, is discontinued, and its steam is not hot enough requiring longer cooking times. I use this one occasionally for rolled oats or some vegetables.

- One [[ASIN:B00019G8IS Oster 5712 Electronic Food Steamer]] - I use this daily for my oatmeal and most dinners. This is still my GOTO steamer in addition to my Secura. This steamer will fail soon as I have had it almost six years and they usually do not last more than that before it burns out. This steamer also appears to be discontinued which is why a once $30 steamer is now being sold for almost $275.

- Three [[ASIN:B000JJMER4 Richard Simmons EST7 Steam-Heat Electronic Food Steamers]] which I absolutely love. These are very large steamers and are larger than the Breville. They have three steaming chambers and are good for steaming full meals (protein, starch, and vegetable) that FINISH at the same time by counting down in reverse. This remains my other GOTO steamer. This is the type of steamer that is not for everyone and which is why it was discontinued due to lack of customer interest. Because I love it so much, I purchased three as I cannot bear to be without one even though I do not use it daily.

- One rice steamer, the [[ASIN:B00007J5U7 Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 5-1/2-Cup Neuro Fuzzy Rice Cooker and Warmer, Premium White]], which is excellent but which I do not use nearly enough. It is also a little different that these other steamers in function so they really cannot be compared.

- One [[ASIN:B003NTXFVG Hard Anodized Non-Stick Wok with Steamer and Lid]]. In addition to this, I also have another very small pot with a steamer on top but I am not counting this one.

- One Stove-top fish steamer similar to the [[ASIN:B0002IBJG4 Norpro Stainless Steel Fish Poacher]].

- One asparagus steamer very similar to [[ASIN:B079DD9115 this one]].

UPDATE: I forgot to attach a picture of the two piece baskets so I am attaching it now.

Nice lettering but the string ruins the look. I really like the lettering on this set (see photo). However, the string provided ruins the look. There are holes in the tops of the letters that need to be punched out and through which this string is passed. The letter H, T, Y, etc. have two holes, etc. However, I feel it would have been best if a gold string-like ribbon were provided instead of this thread as it cheapens the look.

The current price of $7.19 ($7.99 minus 10%) is a bit pricey, especially since only the letters are wonderful.

Fits on all of my pots; works well sometimes; other times it's not so good; size wrong - 2.5 stars. First off, the size listed is incorrect. I ordered both the Medium (this one) and the [[ASIN:B094NBGJNR large]] but just found out that the sizing is wrong. It says this size is supposed to be 9.06 L x 4.92 W x 2.56 H inches for the medium and 8.27 L x 4.92 W x 2.64 H inches for the large which does not make sense because that means the medium is larger. Luckily this one measures at 9.06 L x 4.92 W x 2.56 H inches. I received both of them and they are the same size.

Second, I originally thought this was wonderful because it worked well with long pasta (linguine). Unfortunately, I tried draining tortellini tonight andthe pasta keeps floating above the strainer into the sink. The only way this thing works is if all the pasta stays underneath the strainer and it does not when the pasta is of the small type (think elbows, tortellini, etc.)

This fits on my small, medium, and large pots--even the ones with a slight lip. I just clip it on and then turn over to release the water and hope for the best.

It is BPA-free and heat resistant to 446 degrees Fahrenheit (230 degrees Celsius) and cold resistant to -40 degrees Fahrenheit (-40 degrees Celsius) per the box label.

In summary, I am not pleased with this because the design is such that the pasta can go above the strainer.

Memory Foam in Pieces Pillow; nice pillow; lovely pillowcases. I ordered the small square pillow. It comes with one extra pillowcase besides the one that is on the pillow. The pillowcases are quilted and relativelhy soft and thick. I do like the ear hole as it helps a little when resting on my left side. I particularly love this when resting the back of my head in the hole of the pillow. It is actually very comfortable.

The disappointment came when I opened the pillowcase. The entire pillow is composed of hundreds of memory foam pieces left over from the manufacturing process. It is contained via a thin mesh type cloth similar to what food store reusable shopping bags are made of. This means that if it rips, memory foam will be all over the interior pillowcase and the pillowcase cannot be changed. In addition, about 14 years ago I paid over $80 for two pillows that I thought were solid memory foam and wound up throwing them out after several weeks because the composition shifted making the pillows useless.

I am not saying this will happen with this pillow. However, be aware that this is NOT a solid memory foam pillow. It is made of memory foam pieces.

Despite this, I still like this pillow. Only time will tell if it will last. The current price of $38.89 is on the high side for this considering it is made of what I consider "memory foam waste."

Functional bag organizers to put in a drawer or on a counter; cannot be hung; all are oversized. This is a functional plastic bag organizer that comes in four separate compartments with one each for quart, gallon, sandwich, and snack bags. It also comes with 16 plastic nubs to put on the corners on the underside to keep it from slipping around. Since this is not one unit, it cannot be hung on the wall. The nubs keep these from slipping around on the counter or in a drawer. However, the beauty of this design is that each compartment can be configured anyway one desires. They can go in several separate drawers or in an L shape in one drawer, or side-by-side, etc.

I love the way this keeps all my plastic bags in order. However, there is one other negative besides the fact that it cannot be hung. All the holders are oversized compared to other organizers I tried.

Overall, this is a decent organizer that does away with all those squished and ugly boxes in my cabinets. I do wish it had a frame for at least three or all the compartments so that it could be hung. I also wish they were not so oversized (on the wide side).

The current price of $31.30 ($32.95 minus 5%) is competitively priced for this. However, I personally feel this [[ASIN:B09D5Y63D1 one]] is better if one is looking for four separate compartments. For a variety of organizers (separate and one unit), then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09KMNHM2J one]] or this [[ASIN:B09VGP1WRL one]]. For one full unit only, then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09RF759BM rustic organizer]]. I tried all of these and the style is based on what one desires.

Nice Ziplock bag four-organizer set to put in a drawer but mismatched sizes. There are four individual Ziplock bag organizers in this set. There is one separate organizer each for different types of bags such as quart, gallon, sandwich, and snack bags. This can be placed in a drawer that is large enough to hold it, several drawers, or on a counter. There are 16 silicone circles provided so that they can be affixed in each corner on the bottom to keep each one from sliding around which is great to protect the wall or counter.

Overall, this is a decent organizer set that does away with all those squished and ugly boxes in my cabinets. What I do not like is that this seems to be designed to fit in the shipping box as all but the quarter organizers are oversized. The quart organizer is narrow and tiny. To me this is very odd but it fits well in the shipping box like this (see photo). The current price of $19.99 is reasonable for this. For a variety of organizers (separate and one unit), then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09KMNHM2J one]] or this [[ASIN:B09VGP1WRL one]]. For one full unit only, then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09RF759BM rustic organizer]]. For those looking to store foil and plastic wrap with their bags, then I recommend this [[ASIN:B0B1TPD21S one]]. I tried all of these and the style purchased is based on what one desires.

Sturdy desk but assembly of many parts takes over 2 hours & measurements are wrong. My boyfriend purchased this table for his 27" iMac. I had recommended he purchase a collapsible sewing table instead but he decided on this and regretted it. First of all, it comes in many parts. He tried for three days to assemble this and only got the frame for the side shelves together. I decided to see if I could put this together and it took me over two hours to get the remaining pieces together.

To my boyfriend the instructions were terrible. To me who puts a lot of items together, I found them satisfactory but lacking in certain details. For instance, it never says to install the second bracket or tells the user to face the top small table piece a certain way so that it is flush with the frame. I actually had to remove the top black piece I installed because when it is screwed in one way, the larger desk piece has holes that do not line up. Once I uninstalled the top black piece and then turned it in the other direction, it fit fine. Also, it is important to ensure that the holes in all of the bars are facing as pictured in the diagram.

Once it was together, it looked great as can be seen in my finished photo. However, the measurements online say this is 40"D x 24"W x 30"H when in reality it is 23-3/4"D (front to back--meaning from where the users sits to the wall) x 39-1/2" W (side to side) x 29-1/2" H (bottom to top--meaning how tall it is). First of all they switched the diameter and width measurements on the Amazon site but secondly if we switch those numbers they are 1/2" less on the width and 1/4" less on the diameter assuming they meant to say 24"D x 40"W x 30"H.

In summary, once assembled, this unit is very sturdy and minimalistic and looks very nice. The assembly is long and some people will find that frustrating. The measurements are not as advertised. Also, one of the smaller black shelves had a mark on it from the factory. To me this is 3 stars at the current price of $84.99 plus tax. To my boyfriend, he rates this 2 stars. He was ready to send it back because he was unable to assemble it. Once it was assembled, he is happy with it but does not like that the measurements are slightly off.

Attractive clear organizer to hang on a wall or put in a drawer; a bit fragile - 2.5 stars. This is a simple, basic, understated but nice four-compartment Ziplock bag organizer with one opening each for different types of bags such as quart, gallon, sandwich, and snack bags. This can be hung on the wall or be placed in a drawer that is large enough to hold it. There are four screws and plastic mollies provided for hanging and also four stick-on hooks. The organizer has a hinged front and opens easily as it is held together by small magnets in the corner.

Overall, this is an attractive organizer that sort of fades into the background since it is clear. It also does away with all those squished and ugly boxes in my cabinets. It is definitely an attractive unit even though it is acrylic. However, this is super fragile and does feel like it would break if dropped or handled roughly. I also wish they provided some rubberized "circles" on the bottom to keep it from sliding around in a drawer or scratching a wall. It is due to the fragility of the unit and the lackluster closure of the magnets that I rate this 2.5 stars rounded up to 3 stars.

The current price of $24.99 is on the high side of competitively priced for this, especially since it is thin and breakable. Other options that are available for organizers like this are this [[ASIN:B09D5Y63D1 one]] if one is looking for four separate compartments. For a variety of organizers (separate and one unit), then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09KMNHM2J one]] or this [[ASIN:B09VGP1WRL one]]. For one full unit only, then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09RF759BM rustic organizer]]. For a more modern look, I recommend this [[ASIN:B09WN5PZ6Q one]]. For a larger unit that has room for foil and plastic wrap, then I highly recommend this [[ASIN:B0B1TPD21S one]]. I tried all of these and the style purchased is based on what one desires.

Simple & basic plastic Ziplock bag holder; great for those who love yellow; PRICEY. This is a simple and basic but nice four-compartment Ziplock bag organizer with one opening each for different types of bags such as quart, gallon, sandwich, and snack bags. This can be hung on the wall or be placed in a drawer that is large enough to hold it. There are two plastic stickies with nubs provided but I recommend securing it to a stud with actual screws and mollies and not use what is provided. What I like is that the organizer opens for loading.

Overall, this is an excellent organizer that does away with all those squished and ugly boxes in my cabinets. It is definitely an attractive unit even though it is plastic. The biggest negative is that it is hard to see the etched labels for each compartment. I do wish they provided screws with mollies and some rubberized "circles" on the bottom to keep it from sliding around or scratching a wall. I ordered this for a friend who loves the color yellow and I believe she will appreciate this.

The current price of $36.99 is on the very high side of competitively priced for this, especially since it is plastic. Other options that are available are this [[ASIN:B09D5Y63D1 one]] if one is looking for four separate compartments. For a variety of organizers (separate and one unit), then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09KMNHM2J one]] or this [[ASIN:B09VGP1WRL one]]. For one full unit only, then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09RF759BM rustic organizer]]. For a more modern look, I recommend this [[ASIN:B09WN5PZ6Q one]]. For a larger unit that has room for foil and plastic wrap, then I highly recommend this [[ASIN:B0B1TPD21S one]]. I tried all of these and the style purchased is based on what one desires.

Colorful but thin paper party streamers; difficult to start the roll. There are seven very colorful crepe paper streamers in this package. They are thin but still functional. Also, they are not as wrinkly as other party streamers I've used previously. Starting the roll is difficult and about seven inches of each roll is wasted as a result. Nevertheless, these still work even though they are not great. At the current price of $7.99, this comes to $1.14 per roll.

Unique Ziplock bag organizer w/cutters to hang on a wall or put in a super large drawer but TRICKY. This is a unique six-compartment organizer with two compartments for a box of plastic wrap (or wax paper) and foil with a cutter each and four other compartments for different types of Ziplock bags (quart, gallon, sandwich, and snack). The labels for the bags are etched into the bamboo. There are also two cutter strips included and I installed them in their tracks. The cutting strips cut well as can be seen from my photo.

What is unique about this organizer is that it is expandable. The sides expand to allow me to put the boxes into the organizer instead of just the rolls of foil, plastic wrap, or wax paper. I did not have a box of foil or plastic wrap, so I took a photo with a box of bags in one of the compartments. I also tested the cutting strips with a piece of wax paper ( see photo) and they cut well.

The unit does not open so the bags have to be loaded through their holes.

This can be hung on the wall or be placed in a drawer that is large enough to hold it--the drawer must be very large. No rubberized circles are proved, which is a negative as that is needed to attach to the underside to keep this from sliding around or scratching a drawer or wall. Also, no screws with plastic mollies are provided for hanging, which is another disappointment. There are two holes if using this contracted and for the bags only or four holes if using fully expanded to expose the six compartments.

Overall, this is an excellent organizer that does away with all those squished and ugly boxes in my cabinets. It is definitely a quality unit and a very heavy one at that. However, the BIGGEST NEGATIVE is also its most unique feature. The expandable sections cannot be expanded on the wall. This means, one has to set the expansion distance before securing to the wall. It is also impossible to load and unload the boxes in the side panels when it is on the wall, simply because it cannot be expanded. If they cut a channel or groove where the screw goes, then I would be able to slide it open and closed at least a little bit. It is very possible this has to be removed from the wall every time a box needs to be loaded. Also, if the box size changes, that presents a problem when the distance is already set for a unit that was previously hung.

The current price of $31.99 ($39.99 minus 20%) is on the high side of competitively priced for this. There are many other Ziplock bag organizer options available on the market such as this [[ASIN:B09KMNHM2J one]] or this [[ASIN:B09VGP1WRL one]]. For one full unit only, then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09RF759BM rustic organizer]]. For a more modern look, I recommend this [[ASIN:B09WN5PZ6Q one]] or an individual heavy plastic set like [[ASIN:B09THNTBGX this]]. For a cheaper unit that has room for foil and plastic wrap, then I highly recommend this [[ASIN:B0B1TPD21S one]] but no screws are provided with that one. I tried all of these and the style purchased is based on what one desires. I personally like these other ones a little better than this one.

Stylish iron; runs hotter than expected; wish it were cordless. I own a cordless Hamilton Beach iron that is over 26 years old. It is simple to operate and I love it. I expected this CHI iron to blow me away compared to my old one and to some extent it does but not totally.

I ironed a cotton shirt (see before and after photos in the last two pictures). What I discovered is that the temperature runs hotter than expected as the shirt material was adhering to the bottom of the iron. Therefore, when I put it on cotton, which is what the shirt is, it was too hot. The iron became "sticky" and it was difficult to move even though I used the spray and steam buttons to dampen the cloth. I even tried certain sections not damp but it was still "sticky." Instead I had to lower the temperature to wool in order to continue pressing the shirt.

Also, during ironing, the cord kept getting in the way even though it swivels. However, this is typical of any iron with an attached cord.

When I was done ironing, I had to get the debris left behind from ironing the cotton shirt off the faceplate. That came off easily by ironing over a damp 100% cotton cloth. I also had to clean the iron using the self-clean button. That did not work so well in the sense that water still remained in the iron after self-cleaning was done even after I rocked the iron back and forth over the sink while pressing the button. Instead I had to turn the iron over to drain out the remaining water.

PROS
- This iron is very stylish; it's almost like functional art (see photos).
- The cord swivels and has a Velcro tie for wrapping it up when done.
- The steam and spray buttons work very well.
- The iron is easy to fill with water.
- It heats up rapidly.
- Fabric selection is easily set.
- It is exceptionally easy to clean the soleplate.

CONS:
- The iron runs hotter than typical for the fabric selected. At least that is what I noticed with the cotton.
- The cord gets in the way of what is being ironed; however, that is typical of any corded iron not just this one.
- The self clean button does not steam out all the water as instructions seem to indicate.

In general, this is a nice iron that is almost a work of art. It heats up rapidly and cools down pretty quickly too. It irons well but the cord gets in the way of ironing. Also, the fabric temperature setting runs hotter than expected and self-clean does not release all the water. Nevertheless, it irons well as long as one lowers the temperature. Cleaning the soleplate is a breeze.

Not Working For Me. We get a lot of minimally processed fish and there are often lots of bones to be removed. I thought these would help, but it is very hard to get a grip on the bones without just breaking them off at the flesh. Well made, just don't work for me.

The Perfect Chairs For a Small Area. I got these chairs for the bar in my new kitchen. They were exactly what I saw in my mind. The quality is about what you've come to expect from China for this amount of money. I expect they may last about a year with daily use. Assembly was easily accomplished with one person. They are attractive but a bit wobbly because I think  one of the bases was a little out of round. Overall a very cheaply made product, but it will suffice since there really aren't any other options.
Overpriced But Useful. These are great, the 3 stars are because all of these Command products are overpriced for what they are.

Charging Issues. I've been waiting awhile to review this in hopes that my issue would resolve itself. It hasn't. I love this vacuum except for the fact that sometimes it doesn't charge correctly. I have a small house with 98% hard surface floors and I use this everyday at about the same time to clean up cat litter sprinkles and other light debris. Some days I can do the whole house, no problems. Then randomly I will get one room done and it will stop and need to be charged.  Kind of a bummer. I had a Bissel Bolt Pet, that was terrific until it finally died after years of use. Never had a charging problem with that and it cost half as much.

Sort Of "Useful". Since we are over run with squash right now I decided to try this noodle thing that everyone is talking about. I looked a t bunch of these spiral gadgets and decided, based on reviews, that I'd try this one.

Pros:
Works well doing zucchini and turning it into noodles
The blade storage is handy.

Cons:

Kind of bulky. Takes up a chunk of cabinet space.
No little "tabs" as stated on the box to help you disengage the suction cups. This sucker stuck to my granite countertop and wouldn't let lose.
The instructions are OK, but keep the box because that's the only place the blades are described by function

The quality is about what you would expect for the price. I expect it to last about as long as my fascination with veggie noodles.

Nonstick But That's About It. I'm always looking for an upgrade in kitchen equipment. This isn't one of them. I saw this and mistakenly thought it was like the ones you use in hotels. Not even close. Poorly constructed of the finest plastics China has to offer. It heats up faster than my old iron, but the product produced isn't anywhere near the caliber we are used to. The waffles come out easily, but even at the highest setting they are gummy and not crispy. My old Proctor Silex model takes a while to do a waffle, but they come out as light and airy and crispy as a feather. Besides, this thing takes a ton of space to store!

OK For Light Use. Once again another disappointing appliance. I already have a T-Fal fryer that is awesome. I got this one for those times when you want some more fryer space when entertaining. I knew right out of the box that it wasn't as nice as the one I have. Not nearly as heavy. Could be due to the fact that this one doesn't have an oil reservoir and has to be drained into the bottle after use. Nice digital controls that are really not necessary. If you are frying and setting a time that's not a good thing. Best to always be paying attention to what is in the fryer. I make a lot of potato chips. The directions in the book for this machine say to cook them for 17 minutes. Really!? Talk about burnt to a crisp.

The plug to this is magnetic, like my other one, but this plug won't stay in at all. Barely makes connection and the slightest bump makes it fall out. Not as deep as I was expecting and doesn't hold as much oil either.

The little door that opens in the front to drain the oil is cheap.

It cleans up easily, but I will only be using it on rare occasions. Bottom line, get a T-fal. Better machine.

Heavy and Unbalanced. I really wanted to like this but there are quite a few design issues that prevent me from giving this more than 3 stars.

Likes:
Assembles easily
Dirt cup empties well. No filter in the middle to get everything hung up on.
OK suction out of the box. But most of these kinds of vacs are good for about 6 months before they start to decline in that regard.

Dislikes:
Very heavy and poorly balanced. I have a one level house and by the time I had gone around one room getting the dust bunnies, my shoulder was aching. This thing is very lightweight from the floor attachment upwards. The motor is disproportionately heavy causing a continual struggle to keep the vacuum grounded to the floor. When held at a comfortable angle, the motor practically lifts the floor attachment off the floor. I cannot honestly see doing anything over your head with this.

In that same vein, I put the stair attachment on to go over some furniture. Awful balance. It is a constant struggle to hold this without it trying to turn over in your hand.

The battery when fully charged barely lasted for the 15 minutes it took to go from one end of my house on one level and 3 pieces of furniture before the indicator was showing low.

This will be relegated to a back up vacuum when my Hoover of a similar style dies.

Kind of Low End Quality. A bit disappointed in this product. I have had other items from this manufacturer that were to notch. This is sort of yard sale quality. It is not long enough or deep enough to be of any benefit in my cabinets. I suppose if you have smaller spaces it would be great. It just isn't wide enough front to back and you lose space because of that. Easy to adjust for the height, but doesn't seem sturdy enough to me to hold much weight. Hard plastic shelf that seems very susceptible to cracking. All in all I would not purchase this.

Just OK. This product is just OK in my mind. It seems sturdy enough to at least stack several boxes of shoes at a time. The box itself will hold one pair of shortish boots only, or 2 pairs of shoes. Unfortunately for me I would need a mountain of these to hold the shoes I have. Not sure what the price point on these is, but I think they aren't a really viable option for shoe storage.

I Will Work. Interesting item.  Kind of weird how it works and folds up. Several of the bottoms of the legs were loose in the box on the one I got. Getting them on was tricky. It will do the job for a plastic piece of crap.

Wonky Shape. Interesting. I got a plate to review last week from this same set and manufacturer. I was 5 star impressed. This bowl, not so much. It isn't round and it is very wavy. It may be by design to look handmade, but in any event the shape is kind of odd and strange. Seems well made, just looks really wonky.
Not Great. Poor value. You can get marbles like this at Micheals or JoAnns for a fraction of the price. Nothing at al special about these. Not smooth, lots of chill marks on them and inconsistent.

Didn't Work Well For Me. I've been waiting to have a loaf of bread that these would fit on. They are really rather pre-shaped as if they had used a loaf of bread and then dipped it in the silicone. What I found is that if your bread didn't conform to the shape of this cap, it didn't really seal the end very well and the bread dried out. I really wanted this to work but was disappointed.

Difficult To Use. Where oh where to begin.. I'm not sure that even Mrs. Jetson would have used this.

Pros:
It has a very long cord that makes it easier to use without having to move from plug to plug.
Excellent suction and really picked up a lot of fur and dust.

Cons:
Poorly shipped. This is the only problem I ever have with Amazon. They don't ship large items very well. The outer box this came in was open and had been resealed and was crushed. The inner box with the vacuum was mangled and I had to slit open the whole box to get the vacuum out.

Very difficult to assemble. The instructions are fairly useless. One set on the hang tag suggests one assembly, the manual another. I have assembled 2 level bookcases without as much grief as this vacuum.

For something that is 99% plastic it is VERY heavy and difficult to maneuver. I banged into the legs of all my furniture trying to turn this. I thought that was one of the big selling points for Dyson was their ease of mobility. Not in my experience at all. The big ball does not allow it go under anything.

Emptying the dust bin is a nasty business.

To sum it up, there are a lot of less expensive vacuums with good suction out there. The execution of this machine is way too overwrought.
Does not appear to have any onboard storage for the attachments. Shows some in the diagrams, but I couldn't figure it out.

YES It Slices, BUT.... I was fully prepared for this to not work at all. I make my own bacon and smoked turkey for sandwiches. Cutting the bacon is a pain and I thought I would try this. There are many limitations.

Pros:
It does slice. I partially froze my homemade bacon and it cut it very well

Cons:
Limited instructions. Not much help as far as putting it togther, and virtually none about getting it apart.

Very hard to use. The safety feature on this means that you have to depress 2 buttons and hold them while you are slicing. All this while trying to manage the carriage and feed your food into the blade.

The platform is barely large enough to slice anything meaningful. To do the bacon I had to take the moving parts out of the grooves to make my slab fit on the platform.

The setting for thickness needs to be constantly adjusted. It moves on it's own and before you know it you are getting thicker and thicker.

Exceptional hard to clean. This is the part that worries me the most. The part that folds up at the bottom doesn't come off. Food is trapped in that juncture between the platform and the machine/blade. No instructions on taking the blade off either. But there is a slot in the center hub to lock and unlock the lad. Use a screwdriver and then I used the screw driver to carefully release the blade. I wiped the not removable parts the best I could with hot soapy water on a cloth, and then finally took some clorox wipes and went over all the nooks and crannies.

Very cheaply constructed and I expect this to last no more than a year before the plastic parts crack or break.

All in all, it will cut, but not much more.

Another  Piece of Plastic. Once again an item delivered with no instructions. There are 3 miscellaneous plastic pieces included. Finally figured out that they are supposed to be dividers for the bins. The bins are so small that dividers seem unnecessary. very thin side panels. Not very sturdy. I'm hoping it will still work as a piece of display furniture on my art vending table.
Nothing Spectacular. Just a simple rubber dish drainer. The only thing exceptional is the ability to roll it up and close it. Who does that anyway?

Small. I guess I missed the dimensions in the description. I have several waterfall type burners that are twice the size. This is not big and therefore the effect is diminished. Comes with cones and sticks since there is a place to burn a stick as well. Pointy tweezers which are extraneous. Boring color pallet.  Came backed in a padded envelope so the box was crushed. Luckily not broken.  Extremely boring. Wouldn't buy one on a bet.

Some Issues. This has the potential to be a 5 star item it just falls a little short.

Pros:

Comfortable
Nice cover
Seems well made for the most part.

Cons:
The item I got will not fold completely flat. The headrest is stuck kind of folded over and no matter how I follw the instructions I can't get it loose.
This is very narrow. Only acceptable for a child, thin teenager or smallish woman. A full sized male or bigger woman is going to hang out on either side of this. Also not for very tall people.
The back is kind of sturdy without any support behind it, but it doesn't seem like it will stay in place for very long.
There is also a center of gravity issue with this. If you don't sit in it just right it rolls back and falls over which is dangerous. I was trying this out on a hard surface floor to see if it would move or stay in place, and it flipped me straight back into the coffee table.

Close, but no cigar folks.
Well Made But Fussy. I found this really hard to use. Hard to fill consistently and difficult to unmold. It's such a small little ball it isn't worth the trouble.

Pros and Cons. It looks good once it is together. The together part is the problem. The starter holes for the clamps that allow this to be put together and then taken apart, are marked, but aren't anywhere close to lining up with the holes in the clamps.  That little snafu causes a larger problem. This isn't a folding table in the normal manner. The top is actually a separate piece that needs to be totally removed so that you can fold in the sides. Then you can lay it flat and store the 2 pieces together. THEY ARE NOT CONNECTED.  Because the starter holes for the clamps don't line up, if there is variation in the clamp placement, the top is difficult to get on and off. In fact I didn't think I would be able to get the top on. It would connect to 3 of the 4 clamps. So I took it of and tried it in a different rotation and finally got the top on. That last connection is hard though.  Once it is together is is sturdy, but frankly it isn't easy to take apart and put together. If that's what you are looking for this isn't it.

No Instructions Included. This could have been a 5 star review if they would include some instructions on use besides a small diagram on the box. I figured it out, but it annoys me enough that I deduct stars when I have to do that. I plan to use this for making feta cheese in place of a large press.

Not Like The Picture. These do not fit together like the ones in the picture. There is about a one inch gap between the side piece that slides into the center piece. This means the shelves do no match up and are not the same width. The photo also shows that there are 3 pieces, 1 center and 2 sides, but I only got 2 pieces.  Not very useful and not well made.

Cheap and Tacky, But Pretty Sort Of. This is so cheaply made, I'm surprised it survived the shipping. It is pretty when the lights come on though.  In other words it will look good in the dark. Kind of like a bar at closing time. LOL

Disappointing To Say The Least. Bought this based on the reviews and am now rather surprised that it was rated so high. The only thing I like about this ladle is that it hooks to the pan. I just finished canning some Sweet and Spicy Tiger Sauce and had the biggest mess I've ever made. This ladle DOES NOT fill an 8 ounce jar. It overfills it all over the place. It is also difficult to pour out of from the sides. I'll be going back to my old metal ladle and not making such a hot mess.

OK, With Issues. This product appears to be a really sturdy, functional over the sink organizer. There are, however, a few issues with assembly and quality. The side pieces are tubular stainless, but not very high quality. One of the big selling points is the adjustability of the item to fit most sink areas. One of my telescoping pieces fell apart as soon as I removed the bag, and the second one was jammed together so tightly I had to use a screwdriver to pry the tubing apart to get the center piece lose.
The protective scratch peel on the silverware holder was impossible to remove without scratching the stainless anyway and took longer to get off the whole rest of the assembly.
Versatile ability to set up the spacing and arrangement of the accessories. Be wary of overloading especially if you are putting breakables in the top basket.

Overpriced. This product is well made, but very overpriced for plastic. There is a bag of "hardware" that comes with this. Some is not intuitive as to it's use. The descriptive pictures really don't show you much. I assume the rolls are removed from the box and inserted in the dispenser. There is a round hole in the acrylic panel that defies logic. I guess it is for sticking your finger in to remove the end with the magnets. Could be more user friendly.

Lots of Do's and Don'ts. The first thing that struck me about this pan was the list of things that you shouldn't do to it. The first being no high heat because that will burn off the finish. Don't rap utensils on the edge. You can put it in the dishwasher, but don't. Heat it slowly. So many rules that it is unlikely I will use this very much.
It is well made, pretty heavy bottomed, and does clean up easily. I used it to do some sauteed vegetables and used a Calphalon lid that I had. It did clean up easily and if you don't cook much this is probably a good pan for you. I cook almost everyday/ 365 so I prefer cookware without all the caveats.

Somewhat Better Than The Original Version. I bought one of the original mini Keurigs for my husband's office. It was difficult and no matter what water you used, the coffee always tasted terrible. The new mini has at least resolved the flavor issue. It was kind of difficult to get it to work even after following the specific instructions to the letter. I finally had to unplug it, start over and eventually after raising and lowering the lid several times I got it do the first, cleansing brew. It spit and sputtered, groaned and growled, squealed and screeched, scared the crap out of the dog and then finally spit out some water. All in all a very frustrating and time consuming adventure. Put a pod in and repeated all the previous noises and was finally presented with a passable cup of coffee. Fortunately this is going in my art studio for winter use, because if I had to use it everyday I would probably have to shoot it.
I like the fact on this one that I can take out the water reservoir to fill and clean. The pod storage is stupid because you have to take it in and out to make the coffee. Still not a great design, but some moderate progress. Much smaller profile than the original, thinner and lighter for sure.

Cheaply Made. My first thought when I opened these is that they won't last long. Thin hinges, very cheaply made. If you overstuff the pie and force it shut it is sure to break. No use instruction for the lattice part of the pie and the description page isn't a great help.

Not Very Sturdy. I guess I'm always the critic. I grew up with Pyrex. These bowls are shaped like the little Pyrex custard bowls except they are pretty thin and not nearly as well made.  I will have to figure out a way to keep them separate because the Pyrex could go in the oven and these can't.

Absorbed Food Odors. I was skeptical, but now I'm sold. Very nifty product. I stored my leftover casserole tonight in this and then stuck it in the freezer. I hate the microwave and never use it, so this bag will allow me to place the whole thing in boiling water to reheat. Way to go!! My only difficulty was the opening not being very wide. It made filling the bag difficult and messy. Boy does this thing seal! I got it closed and almost couldn't get it back open. Very impressed.

UPDATE: Used my frozen leftover tonight that was stored in this pouch. It seemed to absorb the smell of the food. It was also very difficult to clean. I ended up filling it with dish soap and water, sealing it and shaking it vigorously. It still isn't really clean. I have deducted a star and would not recommend this item. Stick with glass.
Not the real thing.. Not really a waffle towel. Just an imitation
Disappointing!. It was not as advertised. These were gifts and I  had no time to retur and exchange.
Cushion so so. Cushion not very good
plastic is a problem. The hangers work great!  Only problem is the plastic they put on it will not stay on.

You get what you paid for.. We went for a cheaper comforter bc our dog keeps chewing holes in it, the first time washing it the batting redistributes so that some areas are very thick and others are thin.
Not very good at grinding course salt or pepper. Not very good at grinding course salt or pepper.
Pretty simple looking. For its price it's certainly not bad. But the glasses are pretty simple and primitive. Nothing really exciting.

Overall we love the swing. Overall we love the swing. It took our handyman to put up. There is no back pillow and the seat is very wide- so you feel like you are falling back with no support. We have to add three pillows to make it comfortable.

Nice but flawed. This is pretty well designed but still has major usability flaw: if you fill it all the way to the top, water will start spilling out of the spout because it isn't higher than the pot. The basket design is quite nice and the flip top is well designed as well but come on it's designed to hold hot water and only pour it out when you want it to.

It’s Okay. This is a nice set, comfortable to stand on and looks great. My issues are that the backing isn’t non slip and they pick up every piece of dirt/dust possible. Also the toilet lid cover is just the material with 2 elastic bands to slide it onto the lid, so it doesn’t stay in place very well.

Lights do not work. My advent calendar lights do not work.  Otherwise it is a nice advent calendar.  The drawers are small...only being able to fit a small piece of candy or maybe a nickel in them.  This is very pricey for what you get.

works. Stainless yet, sturdy? Maybe not so much... but they'll work.  We use these when we have our seafood boils.  They do work, but they are a tad flimsy, bendable.  So just be aware that you're not getting heavy duty picks!  Other than that, I do put them in my dishwasher, top basket.  Also, the fork part is SHARP and for that matter the scoop end is rather sharp too...so be careful allowing youngsters to use.

Cheapo made in china plastic... but..... Ok... this is a cheapo, made in China gravy/sauce boat.  But honestly, it will work for my needs.  I am using it for a small amount of melted butter when I do my seafood boil.  It works ok for that... keeping the butter sort of liquid for a couple hours.  Listen, for less than $12, what do you expect? I do wash by hand... the inside cup area is stainless, but the entire rest of the housing is lightweight, cheap plastic. To be honest, I've yet to find one, cheap or expensive that really works.

Dept 56 flying santa. Sadly this worked about twice and then got "stuck" in one position. Disappointing to say the least.  But it fit so nicely above my Dept 56 ornament size village that I just took it apart and glued it the position I liked.  For the money, I was disappointed in the quality, but made it work for me and didn't return it.  I would not purchase again.

hollow plastic easter egg ornaments. The eggs themselves are very cute.... they are perfect for my 2' tall birch tree, about 2 1/2" long... 2 each of 3 colors.  But they came in a lightly padded paper envelope, in a thin plastic tube.  The bottom egg is dented and won't pop back out.  Bummer and very disappointing.  I would look for something a bit more sturdy and shipped much more responsibly.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and I hope this info was helpful to you.

Cook surface is NOT 12". Hmm... I bought this to replace a so-so quality 12" pan with a 2" side. bird bed cover set. I really wanted to love this.. I love the 100% cotton.. the print is really pretty - but a dirty beige background. Wish it were lighter.  The material seems really lightweight. And finally it came removed from its original bag and put into a non commercial vacuum seal bag for mail. There had to be a lot of hands touching it. Eh.  Further, I ordered a second and it was sent the same way.  Disappointing.  I would have preferred it stayed in it's original packing and messing with original seal.  The vacuum sealing did very, very little in sizing. So I wonder why we couldn't have the original bag.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
pikake lei wood candle. Nice scent but a SUCH small candle - the price is crazy.  Disappointed in the price, but the scent is pleasant.

car rug. I have to admit, I was expecting this to be more a carpet top (the print side)... hook and loop? Something... but it is not.  It's like a felt?  But not as heavy - cheap looking and feeling.  It was crammed into a bag and very severely taped in about a 8"x*8" square- so I have laid it out and hoping it will flatten... eventually. I hope this will last one summer and we will move one from it.  Overall, disappointed in the value and quality.

x chef defrosting tray 2 in 1. I apparently misread the ad - it's 2 in 1 - NOT two trays.  Eh.  I am disappointed in that.  But I did purchase this as gift in our family Christmas bingo gift pile.  I will update my review should new info seem useful after someone chooses and uses it.

bread keepers. I purchased these to put some festive holiday loafs in... BUT they are too narrow. Donated all of them and have to come up with a different plan for my gifts.

Roomba i4+. Roomba i4+ purchased off the Treasure truck listing.  So far, a little disappointing.  First off, to get it so sync up with the app - ALMOST impossible. bed tent pirate. Pirate bed tent.  The upside, comes in a nylon bag with good handles and zippered.  The tent is made of a stiff, nylon material. The pirate and space ship version.  They are both 'ok.'

dumpling kit. Well.  I was hoping for a bit more quality - but you get what you pay for... the rounds are VERY flimsy.  The handled rolling cutter is about the most sturdy thing in the kit - the two spreader/filler spatulas are pretty good.  The two wonton/dumpling presses are really flimsy and loose.  I hope they will get through the mini project I have.  They say they are stainless... but if they are, it's the thinnest stainless I have ever seen. Included with the order was a card the says "congrats, you won the prize"  There is a qrl square and a scratch off box that reveals "first prize"... when you go to the website it is a mag subscription (I don't remember what - but nothing good), a whole 6 month warranty, or a $2 "cash" card on your next amazon order. If you make wontons/dumplings a lot - you'll want a much better set.  However, for my use - maybe once? I might be ok.

9x13" pans, NOT heavy duty. 9x13" so called 'heavy duty' aluminum pans. They are not what I would call heavy duty in any way.  I did use 2 on the casseroles I was making in order to be able to lift them in and out of the oven.  If you're using for something that weighs less than 1/2" lb, you're probably ok.  But not if you're planning to make casseroles or ANYTHING with any weight.  They do come with foil lids, which, in my opinion, pretty good quality. Starfish pillow slipcovers. These slipcovers are simply elegant, beautiful! I LOVE mother of pearl and the starfish is beautifully sewn and finely finished. The linen color is definitely what I would call 'ecru' in color. They are just lovely. The look is 10 stars in my opinion.... however... in use, zero stars. I have full, standard 16x16 pillows - sadly, the way the slip covers are sewn, the zipper opening is less than 12 inches (please see photos). So, to get my pillows in the slipcover would have destroyed the covers. They don't begin to fit - even a little. I did think about returning them and reordering the 20x20 size, however, once the pillows would be in the cover (I am assuming a wider zipper opening), they would have been loose and ill fitting - NOT a finished look at all. I contacted the sellers to inform them of the design flaw - their response was less than cordial and in fact demanded proof of the size of my pillows and misrepresented the size of the zipper opening as larger than it is. It doesn't offer the zipper opening info in the ad and probably should. I do really love the slipcovers, but so very disappointed in how much I paid for them only to find I could not use them as I had hoped. I have included photos of the actual zipper opening, less than 12", The standard thickness of my 16x16 pillows, my pillow and lastly a photo of the slip cover laying loosely over the top of my pillow - wishing I could magically make them fit because they are so beautiful. This also shows my pillows are indeed 16x16. Unless you have very thin, fold able pillows (in order to accommodate their tiny opening), I would not recommend these. I am hoping they will update their design or at the very least include more accurate measurement info. I think this comes down to my pillows are not the right kind to be slip covered (their outer cover is not removable) and their design is not useful unless you have a very thin pillow form. For the price, I would have liked to have used them on the pillows I have. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and i hope my review today was helpful to you!
UPDATE: 10/17/2019.. I purchased some thin 16x16 pillow forms and some fluffy 12x12 forms. knee pillows. I purchased 2 of these - one for me, on for big guy husband...  I found it to really too big - awkward and not 'relieving' at all.
