Quality issues. I ordered two of these - one for my living room TV and the others as a hangout place for my cats in front of a bay window. Each had quality issues, and they were different for each of the two.

One had bubbles in the top surface of the "wood" shelf because some of the factory installed fasteners were either too long or torqued too much. Also, the metal legs had rust streaks. At first I thought this was part of the rustic look, but the second one had an even finish. Finally, on the first one one of the bolts would not line up.

The second one had a broken and bent piece of the metal mesh shelf, which I had to cut, then file down. It had two factory fasteners that actually broke the surface of the wood (or laminate) layer of one of the shelves. Finally, the two parts (there are actually four laminate and two metal mesh shelves that are connected to form three long shelves) did not totally line up. From a distance they look fine, but up close it imparts a cheap, shoddy look. Finally, two bolts were stripped, and it was real work lining many of them up.

The sad part is this could have been an outstanding product - other than the quality issues the assembly could have been a breeze (misaligned bolts and shelves aside), and it is sturdy. I'll give it that. And if the quality was there the value would be darn good too.

Personally I am not purchasing another product from this company. Caveat emptor.
Fast shipping. Smaller than expected

Slow, but gets the job done. We got an electric can opener because of a dominant hand injury, so this was really helpful to allow me to keep cooking. And while it was very helpful not to have to open cans on my own, it’s not exactly the fastest can opener.
I normally have to push the button to run it at least twice. It makes about four rotations around the can before it actually opens it. I wish it was quicker. But since I can open cans on my own, this is definitely helpful and great for my kitchen.

Soft, good size, but thin. These are a nice towel set, I liked that it was a set, you get multiple sizes which is nice. The main problem I had with these towels was that while these were decently soft they were fairly thin, like the thinness you would get from a cheaper set. I generally prefer my towels to be a lot thicker than this. I think because of the thinness it isn’t the most absorbent towels either.

Really wanted this to work. I cook a lot but I have a very small kitchen and my pots and pans don't exactly fit comfortably in any of my cabinets, so I decided to get this organizer to help make everything look less cluttered and be more functional. I didn't love the box it came in, and some of the pieces were kind of difficult to get out, they were really stuck on each other. The directions were pretty good and easy to follow, assembly wasn't terrible either. Ultimately, I didn't end up keeping this, it oddly enough was a little too tall for the cabinet was planning on, I found an alternate spot, but honestly it just didn't hold the amount of items that I wanted it too. I ended up finding a different solution and returned this one.

Just eh for me. My house has more lazy Susans in it than I like to admit, in fact I kind of hate them. We have two in on cabinet that we were making for snacks, so I thought these would be a really great way to keep different kinds of snacks separated and organized. I don't like they don't actually nest up against each other fully, they kind of sit at a weird angle so you lose space when you use these. You can really only put smaller items in these. They should have fit in my cabinet no problem, but they were like a half inch to long so they didn't nest into the lip and instead rested on it, so it really just didn't work for my space at all. It is well built, the thickness of the plastic makes me think they would hold up pretty well even with high usage.

Didn’t come with clip. I ordered this for my kitchen. It does what it should do and seems to be durable. The problem I have is it didn’t come with the clip that holds the bag in place. I called to have it replaced and the second one was missing the clip as well. Instead of trying to replace this one I found my own solutions instead of going through anymore trouble. I’ve now have two incomplete trash cans. I do not recommend this company since both the replacement was missing the same piece.

Way smaller than expected, made of plastic. I am keeping this because I like how it looks from afar. However, it was way smaller than expected (burn on me for not checking, I guess) and was made of plastic, cheapening it a bit. Photo has a pen for scale- not quite sure who you’d “serve” on this tray- a hamster or other small mammal?? Certainly not a person
Great sweater and for the wonderful price,. Great sweater. But the is itchy.

Not resistant to cut marks. I had these blue melamine plates that I used as prep boards for years.  You could cut on them but it wouldn't cut into them.  These are okay and like plates which I like (no drip off).  But, I have to put a washcloth under to keep them from sliding all over and they got deep gouge marks just from the first use - slicing potatoes for potato salad.  Not impressed with the gouge marks - they will be a pain to scrub out.
Rather noisy, but works. These are nice, they do seem to clear the air but they are so noisy that I can not use them at night when I sleep - which is what I had hoped to do.

Not sure what makes it cool.... I know the gel is supposed to make it cool.  This blanket is soft and holds my sheet down over me so that I don't need a heavier blanket, so I guess in that way it is cooler.  It could be a little larger.
Teflon film is fragile. Works good, but the Teflon film is fragile. Spoon gentle touch induce obvious scratch mark.

These are just okay. These are mediocre. Hard to clean and egg seems to stick regardless of the amount of oil/spray involved. Still holds and cooks the egg well tho. I have switched back to my single egg frying pan
A bit disappointing.... Guess I was expecting something so wonderful-smelling that I would be blown away.  It’s nice, but not anything special.

Great pan - but the main handle broke during roasting.. Wow - this is one beautiful, BIG frying pan! It arrived just in time to make the spaghetti sauce for the huge family group visiting over 4th of the July weekend. The best part of this pan is the "Helper" handle - what a difference in picking up this pan when it's full. It also is an absolute breeze to clean. We add sausage to our spaghetti sauce, and in our smaller pan, it was always a pain to get the pan clean afterward. No problems with this pan! I had never heard of GreenLife - but the quality is impressive. The lid fits perfectly. Whoever came up with adding that extra handle, deserves an award. What a convenience!

Amended 10/28/16: We have loved this pan and have used it almost daily. Tonight we decided to roast from lamb chops in it (with a basil sauce) and when we took it out of the oven, the main handle broke off - broke in the middle. The information said the pan was oven safe, and we are certain we were within the temperature limits. Very disappointed, as we used this pan all the time. So, if you decide to roast in it, be careful when you grip those handles - particularly the main one.

Interesting design.... This is a mirror that gets everybody’s attention - what’s unexpected is how far it sticks out from the wall - and the side view is not that great. So, best that it be located in an area where it will be viewed just from the front.  It fits into both eclectic and modern decors, and appears well-made.  It could take its place with other wall-hung items to complete an interesting arrangement.

Rather plain - but nice fragrance.... Nice fragrance - don’t know why it is titled “Books”.  It’s also labeled a “homesick candle” which does make sense, as the fragrance is fairly common and probably could remind someone of the home they left behind.  It’s a good size candle and burns prettily.  It’s not unusual in packaging or in the candle itself - it’s rather plain.  Probably a good gift for a student away at school.

Smaller than we expected.. Not what we expected - much smaller - just hoped for a water kettle with ready hot water, without resorting to an electric one.  This one probably has a special purpose, but it wasn’t what we needed.  Looks like good quality, well-made, and the thermometer is a added plus.  Wish it would work for us.

This is huge!  Three feet across!. It comes ready for you to shape it yourself - which will take some time considering the size.  It’s heavy and will be a bit difficult to hang.  It arrived too late to use for Christmas.  If a light goes out, it can’t be replaced - but all the other lights will still work.  Considering how many lights there are, this probably won’t be a problem.  Hanging it high enough to get the full effect is giving us a problem.  Trees are out as we are in our very windy season.  Looks like a project for next Christmas or a very special occasion!

Not soft, but very attractive.... This is a very atttractive throw - but not terribly soft.  It’s completely woven, and looks much more expensive than the asking price.  I immediately thought of all the uses - it could be a tablecloth - a throw on a couch or bed - carry it in the car for seat coverage, etc.  It’s not a throw you are inspired to cuddle up with because of the lack of softness.  But, it is very good quality.

This is something new!. Might take a while to get used to this new way of preserving food.  The “kit” includes reusable sandwich and produce bags, which can be washed, and 3 beeswax food wraps - made of natural beeswax.  They are sticky - and the info included warns us of that - and they are for wrapping around cheese, nuts, fruits, etc.  They can be washed in cool water and reused - and stored in the fridge.  Our jury is still out on the beeswax wraps - as they degrade with time, and we’re struggling to see the gain from their use.  Interesting idea - time will tell.

Not exactly what we expected.... Not very substantial - had hoped it would work as an office rug, but it wouldn’t  stand up for much use.  More of a mat than a rug.  It works well as a mat for an SUV - for pets in the back.  Also good for camping for tent floor since it has a backing that is okay.  Maybe good for a  child’s room with wood floor - non-skid back would be good.  Just disappointed that it wasn’t appropriate for our small home office.

Not the best!. I have a very old central vac system with a very old floor attachment. I thought that this one would be a vast improvement.  Although it fits just fine, the material on the underside that is supposed to catch debris doesn’t really work.  Disappointed with this attachment.

Good and not so good. Love a good egg poaching pan.  This one is just ok.  Its nice looking with 4 egg cups that fits nicely inside with a clear lid.  The eggs cook nicely.  The problem with this pan is the that the handle gets hot so there seems to be a heat distribution problem.  I don't like hot handles.

Not what I thought it would be. This is a nice shower curtain but the fabric is not as rich in color as I expected.  The fabric is stiff, so not as soft as would have liked.  The pattern is ok, but again not exactly what I expected.  This just is not my style.

Good replacement but no instructions. I've had a Dyson for years and it always seemed under powered to me, so I decided to get this and see if it works better. I was surprised when I got the package and there were no instructions. It's not like replacing a battery in a flashlight, you have to take the Dyson apart in order to install the new battery, so it really should come with instructions, which is why I only gave it 3 stars.
I didn't really notice a large difference in performance, so I don't really know if it's more powerful than the standard battery on the Dyson. I wasn't about to swap them out since it does take some time to do that, and so I assume it's as good as the Dyson but not significantly better.
Attractive and functional. Towel bar rocks on the counter. Also, the paint was chipped off one of the top end balls. I would have given this 5 stars, but I subtracted one star for each flaw.

So so quality.. I certainly liked the color and size of these vases but was disappointed in the lack of uniformity the color had around the vases.  The striping on the larger vase was inconsistent in color from the bottom to the top.  Also, the tall vase was a different color blue from the shorter one.  I kept them, but I have to keep one particular side facing the wall due to a defect in each vase on one side.
Grounded, sinking seat.. While the chair is very comfortable you tend to sink into it  if you sit too long. The sitting cushion should be a bit higher and thicker.
Not very tall. Nice, but wish I had gon with larger size.  This not tall enough to cover foods without touching.

Only partially embroidered. I was disappointed to find that only a panel of the cover is embroidered, not the whole top. It's very difficult to see this in the picture, so it should be made clear in writing, or some pictures added. However, in spite of it being much plainer than I wanted, I will keep it because the cotton feels nice and it's exactly the right color.

Not as good as promised.. I spent such a long time choosing a FP and went with the Cuisinart based on reviews AND the photos of gorgeously chopped fruits and veggies. First time out, I tried chopping onions, carrots and potatoes (separately). I pulsed all three perhaps three or four times for a second each, max. No gorgeously chopped veggies. Instead the machine went straight to something one step shy of puree, except for the pototoes, which were uneven and useless, with great big pieces amongst shreds. What a disappointment. I used all the ingredients in a forgiving curry, but it was hard to cook because of the uneven size of the potatoes and the consistency is all wrong. I guess I was expecting much much more from a machine of this reputation and price. I will update if it goes up in my esteem, but for now I'm back to chopping veggies by hand. My old Braun never let me down, but then again I didn't have the expectations I had with this one. Also the Cuisinart website doesn't open. The instruction manual isn't great either and it's difficult to store the blades without investing in more devices. Not sure if I'll keep it or not.
run big. These sheets are nice. I just wish they fit better
Does the job kind of. This rod works but it would not work too good for a heavier curtain. At first it was falling down even after I tightened it.

Not sure this is an actual air fryer. This could be a glorified toaster oven for all I know. I cant hear a circulating fan when I use it. It browns okay but they food doesn't seem to get crispy like it did in my old air fryer.  Still I use it for heating up frozen foods but it doesn't seem to work any better than a toaster oven. One big drawback-it has a timer dial but there are no numbers on it. I turn it halfway for half an hour but haven't timed it to see what the actual time is. Sometimes cheaper is not better.I could hear the circulating fan turn on when I used my old one, (it was a major company one). I don't think this one has one. There are pictures of a few food on top with cooking times but there is no actual timer. You cant turn it a quarter of the way for 15 minutes if this has a 60 minute timer. Don't know because there are no timer numbers, (not even raised bumps for time). Generally dissatisfied. Is easy to clean but definitely not easy to use. I will keep in and use it as a toaster oven but its a little too small for that.
Arrived damaged. The plastic front for this frame arrived scratched. And not just one scratch! Many! Disappointed in this product.
Three Stars. So soft but its listed as a twin and is smaller than a twin

All one piece. It is nice and small for my counter but I don't like the way I can't separate  the two pieces to clean. Update I was wrong about not being able to see these two. No problem  just didn't see it. Plus the water does not leak it goes out the spout just like it is supposed  too.
It works ok. I say it works ok, it make one big stuffed hamburger. And I do mean BIG. It will be fun trying new stuffing of it!
small ball. I returned mine due to it looked soooo much smaller in person even if u read dimensions it seems smaller

It’s ok, not great. It’s an ok desk. It is a little annoying to put together because of the angles of the desk. I used other sturdier screws than what came in package, I also had to make a different more sturdy keyboard holder the track doesn’t 100 percent line up on the one that I recieved as it was slightly bent.
Loud. Fan and remote work well enough but fan is extremely loud.
Pretty Unsturdy. This rack is ultra lightweight but ultra unsteady.  It's really not worth it as a shoe rack.  I'd like to find something else.  This rack won't be holding up very long.
Didn't Find It Quick Drying. It smells a bit when taken out of the package.  The water stayed on top of the mat for a long time.  I'm not sure if it quick dried.

The Coffee Lid Isn’t tight.. Love them and they look great but like other reviewers here the lid on the coffee canister doesn’t seal tightly. Afraid I might move it some way and the lid will come off and spill. Extra careful with it.
Used to be better. Used these for years and my Fuller Brush man retired, so I ordered them from Amazon. Just not the same quality.
Three Stars. Smaller than expected- saw the same ones a bar that could fit a normal beer and these cannot.

Flimsy and not as described. I assumed faux leather meant faux leather and not just brown cloth. Does not look like leather all at and the seams wore out fairly quickly even though I have not machine washed them. Not very satisfied.
Cheap :(. Looks way cheaper in person than in the pictures. I mean, it’s a shower curtian though, so like it works…. Just not as cute as I thought

good enough. it's dull, you'll have to push down really hard, perfect fit for pink lady apples from costco. I tried cutting  bigger apples, the center core is too small, doesn't remove all the core, it cuts into it.

It’s ok. Comes with so many pieces and instructions only include images. Comes with Nails that’s are too long it actually damage the headboard when screwing in the wood part. So be careful … the wood is very brittle. It took hours to put it together.
Measuring Spoons Missing!!!. I gave you a 3 star rating due to the measuring spoons not in there. I will do a better rating if you send me the missing spoons
Not good. Was cheaply made
Not a towel. Small, I wouldn't call them a towel.
Too Big. Wow.  It’s huge.  Makes HUGE ice cream scoops.  It’s nice, no doubt, but large and bulky in my drawer.
Not So Much. The Dragon’s Blood is good; the others are kinda gross.
Three Stars. Very cool but water sits in the bottom.

Helping a Bit...Hopefully Will Help More As Time Passes. Since the age of 2, I experience nosebleeds all winter long. They are like clockwork...as soon as the heat is turned on in the house for the winter, the nosebleeds begin. We're talking every single day; sometimes more than once a day.  We actually have a whole home humidifier but it doesn't work so great. My nosebleeds started up a few weeks ago. I ordered SAFETY & BEAUTY super quiet humidifier with the hopes that using it while  I sleep will stop the nosebleeds. It is charged by a USB. I do like that there is no electrical cord to operate this . Its easy to operate and has 2 levels of output, low and high. It also has has a built in nightlight that lights up in 7 colors.  (neat feature!) It doesn't make much noise at all and is a nice size.  It fits on the night table right next to me without taking up much room at all. I use the humidifier every night when I'm sleeping . Since using it, I'm still having nosebleeds though I have gone 2 days  without one.  I am having some success with the humidifier and I will continue to use it.  Fingers crossed it will prevent nosebleeds or, at the very least, decrease the amount I have all winter long.
Nice lightweight quilt, but pricey for value. It’s a nice lightweight quilt and the silver color is cool but it’s expensive for what you get.
Three Stars. It’s not what I expected but I do like the space for drying scutting board
Okay...... The glass cubes are nice, however, the lids are a problem....sometimes they will lock correctly and "sometimes" I cannot get them to lock.
Too small.... Too small and light weight for a door stop.

Fabric is to thin.. The fabric is very thin. My pillow has a logo on it and you can see it through the fabric. The ruffles lay flat and flop over probably because of how thin the fabric is. Bit disappointed. They were a flop. Haha see what I did there?

Just using for 10 minutes. Product looks great in a photo. I took off the little plastic baby’s breath sprig that is plastic. I also glued on the back better so it wouldn’t come off. For pictures it is fine. For a formal wedding, eh, don’t think I’d use it. Then again, for 5 bucks, I didn’t expect more. Have to say it was super quick shipping! 2 days,thanks!
Not dripless as advertised. Gorgeous candles BUT not dripless as advertised. Had to clean the menorah every night
50/50. If your furniture will stay on them they definitely help, We had to keep readjusting a leg or two as they would slide off.

Read My Entry. The material is nice quality. It came without a tool that was listed. The lip of the lid needs to be sanded because it has many slivers. At the START of screwing in one of the screws, the material cracked. There was a crack in the bottom almost the whole length of the bench. And there is NO WAY it would support 300 pounds. I would return it but I got it for my closet therefore no one will be sitting on it.
Does not measure in ML like it states.. I am very dissatisfied and bought this specifically for the ml weights which is doesn't have
Doesn’t stand well but works. Didn’t stand as well as I had hoped but held up so far

Buy the EVOS German alternative instead.. I just bought (and have been using) both the competing EVOS German-made reusable cloths and also these Trendy Tripper brand Swedish reusable cloths, so I can offer what I hope is a useful comparison.

First of all, congrats to the Europeans: compared to either product reviewed here, our US-made Handiwipes are a joke.

Based on my heavy use over the past couple of days, I have concluded that the EVOS German cloths are FAR superior overall to these Trendy Tripper Swedish cloths:

The EVOS cloths cost only about $8 for 5 cloths.

The Trendy Tripper cloths cost about $17 for 6 cloths.

EVOS are about 14" x 14" in size (and are easily folded if you want something smaller in your hand).

Trendy Tripper are only about 5" x 6".

EVOS absorb far more than TrendyTripper.

EVOS dry out faster than Trendy Tripper.

There is no reason to spend $18 for six of the Trendy Tripper Swedish cloths when you can spend only $8 for five of a much better product.

I hope this helps.

Average quality only.. Average quality only. You can pick up better quality for the same price at an off price retail or like T.J. Maxx. Not worth returning, but I could have done better for the price.

Lightweight rod, heavy finial. The finials are suprisingly heavy for this curtain rod. I like that they weren't hollow. But the rod itself is reeeeeally light weight. The above pix is the rod extended to 47". I ended up putting a piece of electric electrician's tape in the middle so it wouldn't pop out. It hung that way without the curtain on it. Very easy to hang. Took me about 10 minutes. I used included screws, but used a metal drywall anchor.

Fine for travel. Will not replace full sized iron!. Fine little travel iron. But nothing super special. In order to get your clothes pressed decent, you must press the steam button down 100% of the time that you're using it, which is a pain. And may be unreasonable if you have arthritis or other mobility issues with your hands. It's small. It is not heavy. It does not move as nimbly as a full size iron. It does not press as well as a full size iron. But, if you have no space  or you literally iron only 1 or 2 times a year, it would be fine.

These are just ok.. 1st off, these literally smelled like vomit when I took them out of the wrapping. It was so strong, I had to remove them from my bedroom and I put in laundry room to wait for washing. I forgot about them for a few hours and when I walked into my laundry room again, a vomit-smell cloud smacked me in the face and I immediately put them in washer. Luckily, the smell washed out. But they came out horribly wrinkled. I included a pix so you can see how they looked just after I took them out of dryer. I don't use dryer sheets, but do use the wool dryer balls. Also, included 1 pic close up to see color against a true white.

Not my favorite. Shouldn't have ordered this in the height of summer. It came very melted and all the wax was running lengthwise in jar vs on the bottom. I manually mushed it back into bottom of jar. The fragrance is very bold and stayed on my hands for 24 hrs. The sound of the wick crackling makes me nervous. And I'm always looking to see what's on fire. Won't reorder this. And I'll stick to classic candles from now on.

Nothing special. I’m a little disappointed in this glass set. This looks like a boring, small glass. There is a chunky seam on the stem and they look very basic. Too small, really, to use for reds. You could use for rosés or Sauvignon Blancs. I would never re-order these.

Inner seal comes off constantly. Wanted to love this. The plastic is not quite as heavy and thick as I'd hoped. But the biggest bummer is that the gray inner seal on the lid comes off every single time you open it. I've never had a product that claimed to be airtight have this problem.
Already rusted. :(. I've used this for about 8 weeks and it's already rusted at the top. Seals great a d keeps water very cold. Comfortable to hold, doesn't slip. Hard to wash.

These will never be my go-to glasses.. I'm not  WOW'ed by these glasses by Reidel at all. I own many Reidel products and these don't have the finesse I am used to. You can feel a huge ridge where the stem connects to the bulb. It's very clunky and distracting. The stem is thicker than I am used to. Also, the base is super thick and ugly. I included a picture of the new glass on the left and one of my older reidel glasses on the right. The older one has a fluid, 1 piece, thin base and stem. Over all, these feel like an inexpensive libby-like restaurant wine glass. I'm a bit disappointed.

Just ok.. This basket is just ok. It’s a bit too lightweight to be considered sturdy. And kind of small. All 4 castors lock and the wheels move smoothly but they too are light and feel like they might bend off after putting a bag of flour and a bag of rice in this. The entire unit seems to tilt forward too so I’ve had to finagle the wheels even further. I doubt I’d order this again. It was easy to put together though and would fit under sink cabinet as it’s only 19inches tall.

Chunky, kinda ugly. These are heavy, chunky and thick. Looks like something you’d pick up at the thrift store for a dime. They are more a cafeteria style plate and lack elegance. I’d never use them for a special or more formal dinner because they are so ugly.

Split after 1st use 🐝. 🐝 I made soft marzipan candy in these and when I popped them out, I noticed that the mold had split in several places. I included a picture with my review so you can see the weak spots.  I wish it was more durable. The design is darling. And after the bees came out, the detail is spot on and easy to identify. The mold cleaned up perfectly. I loved using this but am disappointed that it may not last long.

Not very magical!. The unicorn is a little scary looking and also has teeth! The chop sticks are a little wobbly. They do not store closed and tend to get stuck in drawer because they are always in open position. Still, they are unicorn chopsticks and my 7 year old is thrilled.

Looks dingy; thin. I love the size and the value of this rug. But it’s so thin and drab. Both my kids asked me if it was old/used prior to us using it because it just looks dirty as it’s normal state. It has no backing. So it needs a pad underneath it if you want comfort. I plan on moving it to the garage after I find a brighter, more cheerful replacement.

Too plastic looking for my liking. This looked more like plastic and less like wicker than I expected. The back of each basket has a convenient hanging tab. The colors are integrated beautifully. I was just looking for something extremely organic and more natural.

Breaks and cracks upon 2nd use. I love the portion of these bowls. They are very easy to initially use, however after freezing a few of them they crack immediately, and after using the second time the lid cracks pretty bad. So I don’t know if I would re-order these, I might look for some thing with a heavier lid.

Almost got it but still not right.. Sadly, my search for the perfect dish drainer continues,as this one won’t work. The main reason is that water pools badly on the drain board and stays there instead of draining into sink. I included a pic in my review. The 2nd reason is because the drain board only drains 1 way so you are forced to set the drainer lengthwise on your counter. And you can’t even push the drainer up against the back wall. The drain board is too narrow and must be aligned with sink. This leaves, on my counter, 3 inches of wasted space between my wall and back of drainer. The expandable drain board is a cool concept. It looks a little wonky but totally works. Love the wine rack and it holds glasses beautifully. I also love the cup rack is over the drain. Gray color is blah.

Attractive but lightweight. This is a pretty table runner. It does have a "modern farmhouse" feel in that there is a lot of texture to the weave, the colors are soft and warm and the runner is a chevron pattern. The runner is 72 inches long and 15 inches wide. The edges are also tasseled. I didnt give it 5 stars because it is so lightweight. It slides all around constantly and has to be smoothed out all.the.time.  As a result, it's barely worth it to use. I have kids who make this runner all bunched up simply by looking at it.

Drips a lot when pouring. Cute black matte finish and sleek design. Comfortable to hold too. But when I pour coffee into my mug, it drips! Not just a drop, a constant dribble. So something is a little off with design. I would not order this again for that reason.
Too short. I wanted a fuller look that when hung in a door, went from door frame to floor. This is much shorted than that and not dense enough for me to consider ordering again

Interesting design.. I give this 3.5 stars. Sure, it’s a futon, but to access that use, you physically need to turn the seat upside down and flip the down. It’s cumbersome and for anyone who is physically challenged, forget it! The bottom has a zippered panel that must be left unzipped when the legs are down. So there’s an unsightly black flappy material under the chair. The back of the chair is black material so you have to have this against a wall or it’s a 2-toned design. It’s only about 8 inches off the green when used as a chair so anyone with knee issues will be challenged to get in and out. As an actual chair, it’s fine. I tend to like former chairs and sofas. It’s firm! And the padding is thin. Overall, it seems best used as a “sometimes”’chair and an emergency futon. You wouldn’t want the pain and hassle of switching this thing nightly.

Flimsy. This is just a so-so press. The metal top does not fit snug in the glass insert, the metal band on the bottom is ultra thin and bent upon 1st use. Because this is a 3 piece unit, the entire thing needs to be disassembled after every use or water will accumulate and get stuck between the glass and the base. I wouldn’t order this again.

Exceptional flavor, challenging mechanics. This makes the best tasting espresso I’ve ever had. Seriously perfect. Like, I almost cry with the first sip every. single. time. I also love the bean hopper and how easy the tamping process is with this. There are many challenges, however, with the rest of the machine. The first being that it draws so much amperage, that it flips the circuit almost every time I use it. We live in a new custom home with a brand new electric system. From the street, to the box, to the wiring. I’ve never had a breaker trip. Even when using multiple large appliances at the same time. It’s a pain. Next disappointment is the steam/wand. It’s really lame. It doesn’t build much steam power and it “pulses” the steam. It takes forever to froth milk. The wand doesn’t have a big enough range of motion to hold a bigger size pitcher comfortably. I ended up purchasing a countertop milk frother that is <<chef’s kiss!>> But again, how stupid that I need an additional step. The last thing is the interface. It works, but not the greatest. We're avid tea drinkers who work urns like these pretty hard, they often get left on for days at a time so we have hot water ready especially in the cold winter months. I have to say, this unit is pretty standard, but seems rather cheaply made. For starters, the spout seems to take FOREVER to pour into a cup. Other urns we've owned can fill a mug with piping hot water in about 5 seconds, this one feels like it takes at least double that time if not longer. It might not seem like much, but when you're making tea for 3-4 people, the difference becomes frustratingly noticeable. Next thing I noticed is that the cord is insanely short. We had to get an extension cord to reach the nearest outlet. I've never owned one this short before.
Then there's the logo. I'll admit, this is purely aesthetic but I kind of hate the logo. It looks so out of place and in a bizarre font that just seems somewhat cringe worthy. The good news is, it seems very cheaply printed onto the metal and actually comes off with a FINGERNAIL scratching at it. That's good and bad however- its good because I was able to remove it easily with my thumb nail, but it also makes me wonder what would happen to this if exposed to the heat of the unit running for a prolonged amount of time. Like, would it burn off and/or smell? If it comes off that easily I don't have high confidence in the quality of the printing. Then there's the temperature. I don't know exactly how hot it is, but it seems less hot than some of the other urns we've used. For things like tea and instant oatmeal, its fine but when I made coffee and then added cold milk, it already lost the piping hot effect I was hoping to have to warm me up in the morning. It simply isn't starting off hot enough to add cold milk to it and remain hot.
In a nutshell, it works and does what it claims to do. But for the money, I think there are better options out there.

Decent ceramic burr style, could be better. After reading a lot about burr grinders, I was excited to give this a try. However, with no prior experience, I found the lack of proper instructions to be very frustrating. It comes with a paper booklet but it is written very poorly and does not at all make it clear how this is supposed to work. Thankfully, I found someone on youtube demonstrating a product that looked almost identical. The top of the unit opens up around were the handle attaches, and beans can be put inside. The bottom half (with the window) holds the ground beans, which can then be poured easily into the filter for brewing. In between those is the ceramic grinding parts, with a knob that can be adjust to make it more fine or more coarse. This in particular was very unclear in the instructions, as it almost sounded like turning the crank clockwise or counter clockwise would effect the grind, but it mean this adjustment gear.
While loosening the adjustment gear to see how coarse it can go, it actually popped off and the entire assembly sprang out into a few different pieces (thanks to a tension spring that is supposed to hold it all into place. I managed to get everything back together to a point that it seems to work, but once again, the instructions did not warn me not to turn it too far, and it really could have come with a diagram or something to reassemble it as I'm still not 100% it was assembled properly again after that.
Bottom line is: It works. But it is NOT beginner friendly at all.

Its OK for a starter kit, the press is the only good part. The appeal of this kit is that it comes with everything you need (and even some stuff you don't) to see if you like the process of making French Press coffee. Honestly as a kit its ok but none of the components are all that great on their own. The burr grinder is one that I've seen before and disliked- very hard to use correctly and breaks easily. Even in the video that they show on the product page, notice how they fade to cut time when you see the user grinding. He even looks like he's struggling at first, and then the editor is like "nope, let's cut ahead some time!". The other included accessories such as the milk cup are cute, but honestly not necessary. If you have a milk frother, you're not going to pour it into this first to then pour into your coffee. And if you are using your milk straight, again, why pour it into this? For aesthetics? To serve? Maybe I'm just missing the point of it, and there aren't really instructions to clarify.
The actual press is the only part I like. Some die hards will tell you to only make it in glass but the metal container is perfectly fine IMO. The press is a little bit smaller than I'm used to, so it is only good for smaller portions of coffee, but the filter is interesting and easy to clean, which I liked.
All in all, its ok because it comes with so many things so it might make a cute gift, but I feel like you can get much higher quality versions of all the necessary components for not a lot more money. I'd rather buy a better grinder and bigger press separately, and skip the other things.

It's ok. Filter lasts about a month.. Physically, what I don't like about this pitcher is that the little "handle" they put in the lid so you can lift it off is pointless. The lid snaps in, and the little groove you're supposed to grip to lift it off isn't nearly sufficient. So you end up sticking your finger in the end where the water comes out, which I don't really care about but someone might if they're very concerned about germs.
Secondly, the pitcher really doesn't filter much at a time. Even if you fill it once and then refill it again, the second time the water takes so long to filter that it's just easier to do it one at a time.

I like the way the water tastes when it's filtered. It's not for everyone. It's like how it tastes when you buy bottled water that's been "mineralized for taste", which really confuses me since this supposed to filter out most things. But whatever--I still like the taste of it.

However, I actually bought this not to drink with but to water my plants and fill my humidifier. I have a few sensitive plants that demand distilled water, rain water, or super filtered water like this (living in the desert prevents me from collecting rain water). Since I don't have to water my plants a lot I'll probably keep using it for that.

I was using it to fill my humidifier each night to prevent the "white dust" that can settle around humidifiers and also prevent hard water build up inside it. It was certainly effective, but I had to use so much water just to fill up my humidifier each night that I used up the filter fairly quickly. I filled the pitcher probably 3 times per day for my humidifier, plus add in a few extra fills for watering my plants, and the filter lasted about a month.

After about five weeks of using my humidifier with this pitcher, my humidifier started smelling fishy, which I thought was strange considering I had just cleaned it the week before. I ended up cleaning my humidifier multiple times and refilling it thinking it was my humidifier at fault, but I was wrong. I finally thought to smell the water that was filtered from the pitcher and it was the water that was smelling fishy. So obviously the filter had run its course. I tested with the TDS meter just to see what the filtered water was at, and it read 088.

Considering these filters cost over $12 a piece, I am not going to continue to use the pitcher to fill my humidifier. I'll just deal with the hard water consequences. I will continue to use it for my plants and I'll probably start drinking it since I liked the taste. I'll be interested to see how long a filter last doing that.

Good loft bed, but some shortcomings that prevented this from being 5-Stars.... THE GOOD:
--------------
* Very professional product.
* Instructions are easy to understand, but you must be attentive and don't skim, or skip ahead.
* Great space saver if you feel your room is a little small.
* Aesthetically, very modern with rounded corners.
* Built in shelf design, as well as a hanging rod for clothing.

THE BAD:
------------
* Parts of the assemble are so tedious. Your fingers will hurt snapping in a bunch of plastic tabs.
* One of the set screws in the frame came loose, so I couldn't unthread a screw. This should never happen. So I'm not too thrilled that I had to spend 30 minutes fixing it.
* The designers or engineers obviously never used loft beds because if they did, then they would have known to make the ladder comfortable to step on. The round ladder steps were a TERRIBLE choice. You'll need to add foam to it.
* Do all loft beds wobble? I don't know, but this one does.
* Guard rail is about 11" high. My son's mattress is 8" thick. That leaves 3" of protection. I don't feel comfortable with that. We will get him a thinner mattress.

In conclusion... for a such a professional looking product, I was really disappointed in the fact that it wobbles, the fact that I had to fix a loose set screw, and how they put no thought into the ladder design. I will rate this 3-Stars overall.

They don't give you enough magnets.... THE GOOD:
--------------
* Universally sized so it should work with most home washer and dryers.
* Keeps clothing from falling off the back.

THE BAD:
------------
* Not enough magnets. Sure they're earth magnets, but they're small and spaced too far apart. There needs to be more of them. I think the bottom should be one long strip of earth magnet. Actually, I bet you that it doesn't have to be earth magnets. It can be standard tape magnet, but if it's continuous and covers the entire bottom rails, I bet you that would be stronger than small earth magnets that are spaced far a apart.
* Moves easily. You can flick it with your fingers and the entire wall wobbles. Again, this is due to not having enough magnets.
* For best strength, DO NOT connect the middle. It just so happens that in my situation, I need to split the middle anyway because there is a shelf bracket in the way. But even if I didn't have this shelf bracket, I would still split the middle. The reason is because if you connect the entire thing, then the entire width will be much shorter than the entire width of both your washer and dryer. The top of washer and dryers machines will also vary in design, some have raised edges, which makes it tricky to make sure all the brackets are connected on the same raised level. So I just split it up. This way, it's easier to manipulate how and where I want the brackets to stick. This may sound confusing, but you'll see once you buy it.

Overall, this is a so-so product. Every day we're fixing the brackets cause it gets moved a lot. So it's doing it's job in terms of not letting your socks fall off the edges, but it is not sturdy. I will install extra earth magnets when I have the time. I'll go 3-Stars.

Just purchased my second one .... My first one was purchased in late 2008, and was used 4 or 5 times a month. It finally broke this morning trying to open a badly stuck jam jar lid. Four years of use for less than $20: yep, I definitely got my money's worth.

My first one could be a tad "finicky" at times, but it ALWAYS worked fine on everything from pickle jars to home-canned jars. Also, it's rather particular about battery strength, so bear that in mind if you use yours a lot. If the batteries are weak (but not yet dead), it might not be able to remove a particularly tight lid.

I'm hoping to get the same performance out of this replacement.

UPDATE 10/25/2013 ....
My second one broke this morning while opening a jar of preserves. They definitely are NOT making them like they used to. My first one was a champ; this one opened maybe 10 jars before breaking. It was good while it lasted.

Bottom line: if you're going to open only jars that aren't too tightly closed, this might be OK. But I just ordered a "manual" opener as a replacement. I'm done with the "automated" ones, arthritis or no.

Stylish look, but useful for light duty ONLY .... Very mixed feelings about these.

First, what'd good:
== size -- they're perfect for getting that last bit of mustard from a jar or stirring a bowl of creamy dip for a vegetable tray
== appearance -- very classy looking: gray silicone heads and stylish stainless-steel handles
== the silicone heads can be removed for cleaning

Now, the problems:
== the silicone heads do not fit tightly onto the stainless steel handles, so if you're trying to get that last bit of jam or preserves (or anything sticky), the head will slip right off
== the spoon head is very pliable, so it can't be used for any "heavy lifting" or scraping with anything more than very light force.

I'll definitely get more use out of the mini spatula rather than the spoon -- it's just too flimsy to be useful for anything but the lightest duty. Before I could give this set more than 3 stars, there would need to be some serious redesign so that the heads don't slip off so easily, and they can be strengthened to allow for more versatile use. I think they're OK -- but nothing I could really recommend at this time.

Just OK .... This is probably an OK product for a first French press coffee maker, or one where it will get light usage. But it just feels "flimsy" to me -- the glass carafe is very thin.

I can't speak to the long-term durability, as I've only had this for a couple of months and I've used it probably 2 dozen times, but it seems to be holding up OK. The filter part of the press is looking a little worn, but then I usually take it apart to clean after every use. It makes a decent cup of coffee (don't let the "6-cup" designation fool you; this makes a maximum of about 28 oz of coffee, which is just over 2 standard-sized mugs), once you figure out how coarse/fine the grind needs to be.

I like the flat-topped plunger -- I have two other French presses, one with a "ball"-style plunger, the other with a small knob, and this one is definitely easier on the hand.

If you're looking for a small French press to try out the idea of French press coffee, this might be a good economical choice. But if you're looking for something to handle daily heavy usage, you might want to spend a few more $$ and get something larger and more substantial/sturdy.

High quality, but usefulness? maybe not so much .... I've owned a couple of other "handheld" spiral cutters and currently own the larger hand-crank Paderno spiral cutter. So I've had some experience with these devices and eat spiral "noodles" a couple of times a week.

First, if you've never owned a spiral cutter and you're thinking of trying one, this might be a good choice. Much better design than most handheld units, easier to set up and operate, etc. It's a bit pricier than the cheaper ones, but the better design makes it worth it. It handles softer veggies (zucchini, cucumbers) fairly well, but you do have to be careful of the diameter. Still, it might be a good intro to the sport/art of cutting veggie noodles

If, however, you have experienced the pleasures of a well designed "crank" style spiral cutter, you will be very disappointed in this. The size makes it difficult to do larger veggies (sweet potatoes, rutabagas, etc.) without serious paring down to fit the small opening. Also the effort needed to twist the holder with the veggie is not trivial. As someone with shoulder and hand arthritis, I had difficulty with this.

Even if you've never used a spiral cutter, it might be worth it to add a few bucks to the cost of this and go for the other Paderno hand crank cutter. It's so much easier to use and you'll have more options (with less waste) of veggies to cut. I've been using the larger Paderno cutter a couple of times a week now for about 6 months, and it's going strong with no sign of any failure. Paderno makes quality stuff, and this little cutter appears to fit my quality expectations for the brand. Pity it's not more useful/easier to use.

I'm giving this an "It's OK" rating -- 3 stars. Just not that useful for me; might be a good intro to veggie noodles for a novice.

OKAY BLENDER FOR THE PRICE; A COUPLE NICE FEATURES, ATTRACTIVE. The first thing I noticed about this blender is that the blending cup seemed very short and it seemed like it wouldn't hold as much as my other blender which hold 5 cups and is taller.  This holds 6 cups and the reason it can hold more without as much height is that the blending cup is bigger around.  The cup is nice thick glass and is one of the better features of the blender.  The blender is attractive, with a silver colored base, but the base doesn't appear to be metal, but more like a pastic coated with silver material.  Seems powerful enough to do most jobs, but probably more of a light duty blender.  The wattage is 550, which seemed like a lot, but in checking other blenders some are in the 700 to 750 watt range and I'm sure they go higher as well.  The gasket is not a separate piece which is a real plus.  I suppose 12 speeds is nice, but how many speeds do you really need?  I don't even use the 8 speeds on my old blender.  Instructions say that to blend hot liquids you need to leave the cover loose and cover it with a towel.  Seems like a hassle when other blenders will handle hot liquids without doing anything special.  When using it with hot food and liquids, you'll now have a dirty towel to wash.  I usually don't read what other reviewers say, as I don't want to be influenced one way or another, but I noticed several who had a problem with the plastic blender cup base breaking easily.  With a two year warranty and the low price of this blender, you probably can't go wrong, but it's not fun to wait for replacement parts.  You also have to search for your receipt and whatever else might be required for warranty service or return.  If I wanted a quality power tool, I wouldn't think twice about selecting Black & Decker as they make good power tools.  Are their small appliances as good?  Probably not.  I recommend buying a blender from a manufacturer who has a long history of making quality blenders.  Apparently Black & Decker acquired General Electric's small appliance division in 1984, so it would seem they have over 20 years of experience, but contrast this with the Waring Blender company that has been making blenders since the 1930's.  There are so many blenders available in the market and there probably isn't a lot of difference amongst them until you start getting up into higher prices.  Seems like there is a lot of competition in the market for blenders and this is a low end competitor is good enough for people who don't use a blender every day.  If you are constantly using your blender (like for a daily smoothie), select something more rugged that costs more.  This is by no means a food processor; I think it is wise to spend more and get a combo food processor and blender, which should serve your needs longer.  This is probably good for a cheap, attractive gift, especially for someone just starting out who really needs a blender.

Quality Chair; easy assembly; works good. This is a little better than a basic office chair. It was easy to assemble. Probably didn't take more than 15 minutes. Includes an Allen wrench which is the only tool you need to assemble it. It is reasonably comfortable. I haven't tried sitting in it all day, but seems fine for several hours.
At first I thought they had sent the wrong seat, as the holes didn't line up on the bottom of the seat for the bracket for the back. They do line up, but I had the bracket in the wrong direction; it only works one way, so you can't make a mistake on assembly. I would have preferred a chair with arms and I think this same chair must be available with arms, as there were mounting holes in the seat for arms. If you buy a chair with arms and don't want or need the arms, you can always remove them, but it is nice to have that option. This model doesn't have the arms and that's okay if that's what you are looking for. If you spend a lot of time in front of a computer, as I do, you probably want a better chair, but this is a good chair, especially if you aren't sitting for hours. I would probably buy it again if I needed another chair, but I would opt for the model with arms next time.

After using an individual cutting board, before inserting it back into the storage rack, you need to make sure it is really clean or food particles could fall down into the rack.  Of course normally you would clean a cutting board after use anyway.  If you don't want to worry about a complete cleaning of a cutting board after using it, you could use all four boards for anything you want to chop and then after use, put each in the dishwasher after use.  When all 4 are dirty, you run your dishwasher load and then restore 4 clean cutting boards to the rack.  Definitely some good advantages to having 4 cutting boards in a slim attractive rack instead of just one all-purpose cutting board.

A big step up from bargain toasters.... I spent years in graduate school making do with a five-dollar toaster. After moving into my first home, I decided it was definitely worth the splurge to upgrade to a toaster worthy of my homemade breads. I was given a KitchenAid 2-Slice Toaster as a housewarming gift, and the love affair hasn't stopped since.

The KitchenAid performs all the usual functions of a toaster, with many choices from light to dark, but also features a bagel setting designed to toast the cut side of bagels more thoroughly than the crust, and a "warm" setting to keep your toast warm without turning it into charcoal.

The toaster has a nice solid construction, with heavy-duty metal parts and a well-built crumb tray that slides out, eliminating the mess from trapdoor-style crumb trays found on cheaper toasters.

Since I bake my own bread, I tend to slice it thickly, and it turns out perfectly in the KitchenAid. But beware: if you use store-bought (or other thinly sliced) breads, the extra-wide slots mean that your toast may turn out very light and need an extra toasting since the bread is held further away from the heating elements. But it performs beautifully on bagels, English muffins, and thick slices of bread. Whoever said that man cannot live by bread alone failed to toast it in a KitchenAid toaster!

Pros
Toasts evenly, bagels come out perfectly done

Cons
Sometimes frozen breads require extra toasting, warming feature ineffective

Authentic Italian espresso at an affordable price. After many happy (and dare I say, naive) years with our DeLonghi Caffe Espresso, it was time to replace our old workhorse. Having just spent the summer in Spain, where no bar is complete without the standard superautomatic Gaggia espresso maker, I decided that truly great espresso was a daily necessity. I was tired of incompetent teenagers / college students who work at local coffee shops mangling something as simple as a cappuccino (one part espresso, one part milk, one part foam) into a milk-drowned latte with no foam.

I wanted something in the range of $200, with a dependable track record and plenty of power to spare. I waded through a myriad of reviews for the Gaggia Carezza, hailed as a champion of its class, but read a number of negative reviews concerning design shortcomings.

Enter the Gaggia Evolution. Although the Gaggia Carezza and Evolution share the same innards, the Evolution boasts several improvements in design. With its 17.5 bar pump and high wattage, dual element boiler, the Gaggia Evolution is ready to brew in around 5-10 minutes (I always prime the boiler first).

Design improvements over the Carezza include: a larger drip tray, a cup warmer (although, as usual, it's more effective to preheat your cups by filling them with hot water, which can be done during priming), anti-vibration mounts (once primed, the Gaggia Evolution is nearly whisper-quiet), and a brass commercial portafilter (the spouts on the Carezza were changed to plastic). My Evolution came with the Perfect Crema device (which is supposed to go under the single filter basket in order to create additional pressure/allow a coarser grind), but having read numerous negative reviews of the ineffective device, I simply left it in the box with the packing material.

Five stars for the instruction manuals and CD-ROM: the Gaggia Evolution comes with not one, but two instruction manuals: one from the manufacturer (Gaggia), and one from the North American importer (Importika). The Importika manual is intuitive, easy to read and injected with coffee humor, although the Evolution is not among the Gaggia models listed in the Appendix. The included CD-ROM walks you through setup in the form of short movies and narration, along with more advanced tips and techniques for coffee connoisseurs. We put our laptop on the kitchen table and followed along after unpacking our new Gaggia (thankfully, nothing was broken in the mail, as happened to several Gaggia Carezza owners). Although the manual hinted that your first coffee might not be potable, we'd followed various tips online (prime your new machine several times to remove any residue and plastic-y taste), and our first espresso was laden with crema. The Turbo Frother attachment made the creamiest, densest microfoam I have ever seen-it looked more like meringue (hint: use skim milk for best results). My only complaint would be the cheapness of the included coffee scoop, and you definitely want to invest in a better tamp for maximum extraction (the Gaggia takes a 58 mm tamp at a recommended 30 pounds of pressure).

If you're not in the market to buy a $200-300 grinder (Rancilio Rocky or Gaggia 8002 MDF Burr Grinder) to go with your new Gaggia, Illy makes a delicious, dependable espresso grind, available in tins (decaf, too) or Pods. The Evolution is Pod-ready, simply use the single shot basket with the portafilter. Tip: "classic" double shots should take around 20-25 seconds to extract.

The Evolution is a steal for the current price, since it contains the same innards as other Gaggias in the $400-500 range. Although it runs around $50-100 more than the Carezza, I appreciated the design improvements, stylish lines (I have a Tuscan kitchen with hand-painted ceramics and terra cotta tiles and was afraid that the "modern" styling would stand out, but the Evolution is much more traditional-looking and unobtrusive than the Carezza), and performance. (Note: the Evolution is also available in an all-silver model, but it will set you back another $50. The black model features a black base and sides and a silver front and silver drip tray.)

Excellent for the espresso novice or connoisseur, easy to use and clean, and it makes better espresso than some $500-1,000 machines I've tried!

Recently, I moved into my first home and was given a set of four heather four-piece place settings. I plan to add on to the collection as more pieces are added in the newest color, heather.

This four-piece set comes with a dinner plate, salad plate, stackable cereal bowls, and a mug in place of the teacup and saucer present in the five-piece place setting. Besides being durable (it's dishwasher, microwave, and oven-safe), lead-free, and coming with a 3-year chip warranty, Fiestaware has been made in the USA since 1936.

The classic Art Deco styling and wide range of coordinates (vases, teapots, trays, candlesticks, spoon rests, salt and pepper shakers) means that it?s fabulously easy to mix and match various colors for an eye-catching effect. The dishes are substantial in weight, and make a striking presentation for any meal. Fiestaware is an excellent investment and the perfect wedding or housewarming gift.

Keeps your butter cool, fresh, and ready to spread. Emile Henry Auberge butter pots are the perfect addition to your breakfast table or afternoon tea. It holds 8 oz. (one cup) of butter, plenty to satisfy the whole family at mealtimes. No more rock-hard pats of butter when your toast or rolls are ready! Plus, this new color (figue) coordinates beautifully with Fiestaware's heather dishes.

A baking powerhouse with lots of great added features. The Breville 5-Quart Die-Cast Stand Mixer is my second stand mixer. I'm a heavy-duty home baker, so I need a durable stand mixer for creaming and whipping (I knead bread doughs by hand rather than in a stand mixer or food processor, which is the surest way to burn out a motor).

Setting up was a breeze. You simply push the button on top to tilt the mixer head, attach the desired attachment, lower the mixer head, and you're good to go. I appreciated that the mixer head has a very sturdy locking mechanism; there's no wobbling when you have the mixer head up to add / switch attachments. I also liked the handy "handle" on the front. Even with the mixer on medium-high, there was little movement of the unit.

I was thrilled that the Breville came with a scraper attachment; my first mixer was a Kitchen Aid, and I spent a sizable sum buying a nearly-identical attachment that wasn't included in the box. Just like with my Kitchen Aid, sliding and locking the various attachments is intuitive. There is also a dough hook, a wire whip, a metal flat beater, a rubber spatula and a pouring shield. I also liked the fact that the grounded plug is shaped like a doughnut; there's a hole in the middle so you can use one finger to pull out the plug if your hands are covered in flour, chocolate, etc. without getting the whole plug dirty.

Another feature I really liked was the ten-minute digital timer and the "pause" function (with my old KA mixer, you'd have to turn the mixer all the way off; a pause setting is really handy). And because the speed controls are digital (there are 12 speeds total), there's no grinding or sticking of gears (my mom went through *three* Kitchen Aid stand mixers under warranty due to stuck speed control levers and mixer gears).

This is an excellent choice for novices and pros alike.

This would make a super-cute housewarming gift or wedding gift paired with my friend Maureen Abood's hummus starter kit, available from Maureen Abood Market, as well as a copy of her excellent [[ASIN:0762454865 Rose Water and Orange Blossoms: Fresh & Classic Recipes from my Lebanese Kitchen]].

Great durability + vintage design = classic Corelle!. Like many others, I grew up with several sets of Corelle dishes in my house, including pansies and the Christmas scene set, as well as coordinating bakers and accessories. So it was with no small sense of nostalgia (as well as a sense of pride that this line is still made in the USA) that I snapped these up (after moving into my own homes both stateside as well as overseas, the original set of Corelle is still in my childhood home). Oddly, these are not listed as Corelle plates, but most definitely are as they are marked on the back.

The weight and quality of these is on par with vintage Vitrelle glassware, and the decals are evenly placed (Corelle is dishwasher safe, but cannot be used in the oven or broiler). They are listed as chip and break resistant, and from long years of experience using Corelle (and dishwashing), it's quite likely the decals will eventually wear off, although the plates themselves are still serviceable 25+ years later. I also love that the manufacturing process uses 65% recycled glass. The packaging was very straightforward; all six plates were nestled into a slim cardboard box.

As a single household, this is the perfect-sized plate for me (I prefer serving meals on appetizer and salad plates as mealtimes largely involving mezze and grazing). They work well for serving appetizers, desserts, sandwiches, etc, and the retro print would be great fun for a potluck, mahjong gathering, or retro-themed party. These would also make a great gift for a new college student starting off on their own; I love the versatility, durability, and most of all, the fact that you can still find dishes made right here in the USA!

Three good things...and the one knife to own. Santoku knives are currently very trendy in the foodie world. One only need watch Food TV for one or two shows to see the myriad of TV chefs that use the santoku (Japanese for three good things) to slice, dice, chop, and scoop ingredients into the bowl.

Traditionally used as a chef's knife in Japan, the hollow granton edge creates extra pockets of air that prevent thin or soft slices from sticking to the blade. The knife has an excellent balance and a heavy weight in the hand. I would recommend using the Wusthof ceramic sharpener to restore the blade to its factory-original sharpness. Wusthof's Classic Santoku is expensive, but a worthwhile investment for your kitchen.

An essential for frosting and layer cakes. If you're a baker who frequently makes brownies, bar cookies, and cakes, you need to have an offset stainless-steel icing spatula in your collection. The blade is the ideal combination of strength and flexibility, and using an offset spatula means that you don't end up dragging your knuckles through your frosting as you work around a cake. It's useful for leveling brownie and cake batters to ensure even baking and is a must-have for spreading frosting, particularly on quick-setting sheet cakes like Texas cocoa cake. It's also my tool of choice for spreading fillings and frosting layer cakes. When you're finished, you can either hand-wash or pop it in the dishwasher.

Five stars for versatility, four stars for plastic and fflimsy rubber. I waded through a myriad of blender reviews before settling on the Oster 6-in-1 Stainless Steel Blender. We used to have a vintage Oster beehive blender from the 1960s, so I knew that it was a brand with a good reputation. The biggest appeal of the 6-in-1 is its versatility: besides the blender jug, it also comes with a milkshake blade and stainless milkshake pitcher, food processor, and baby food jar.

The motor drive is metal, and the blender base is stainless, with a very solid weight to it. So many of the other blenders I researched had plastic gears and components and looked as if they'd break the first time I used them. With 550 watts, this is more like a jackhammer that quickly and effectively makes short work of ice cubes. There are only three basic speeds, and I've found that pulsing works best, as the motor may work overtime when you're only blending a small amount. Unlike some reviewers, I didn't find the Oster's motor to be as noisy as claimed.

I've used it to make milkshakes and breakfast smoothies (ice cubes, almond milk, yogurt and frozen berries), and also used the included food processor attachment to make a small batch of artichoke dip (artichoke hearts, garlic, lemon juice and mayo). I have many recipes that will make good use of these additional features. This is a good deal for the money, as it is capable of more than simply blending. I only wish that some of the additional components were built of a sturdier plastic (the rubber gaskets are flimsy as well).

I'd previously ordered the NordicWare Bee Cookie stamps and loved them, and the Starry Night cookie stamps don't .... I ordered these after seeing them featured on King Arthur Flour's website; I'd previously ordered the NordicWare Bee Cookie stamps and loved them, and the Starry Night cookie stamps don't disappoint. The three gorgeous Nordic-inspired designs will be sure to dress up your holiday baking; they work particularly well with gingerbread (there is a recipe included on the box; I opted to use King Arthur Flour's Winter Spice recipe (see comment below).

Be sure to wash the stamps thoroughly the first time before use, and to dry thoroughly; it's normal to see a light layer of grey come off. Do not submerge the wooden handles in water.

It took a few tries to get the hang of using these; one recipe recommended rolling out the dough to 1/4', stamping, then cutting, but I opted to roll the dough into 1-oz. balls, rolled in sugar, then stamped.

Be sure to use a nonstick spray and/or flour your stamps generously between cookies. Stamp until you can see the edge of the dough peek out from under the stamp, then I found that twisting and lifting, the stamps separated easily.

Once cookies were baked and cooled, I used Wilton Pearl Luster mixed with ginger liqueur to paint the tops, and they are gorgeous enough to be hung on a Christmas tree and make a stunning addition to your cookie tray.

medium size egg coddler. So these are "medium size" and will hold 2 eggs - traditionally you coddle one egg in a smaller cup, but this will work.  Remember "coddled" eggs are NOT poached.  They are delicious alternative to poaching or other water cooking.  Rub the inside of the coddler with generous amount of softened butter or olive oil.  Seal the lid top and place in boiling water pan (water below the lip of the coddler).  Cook per your desired temperature.  Around 10 minutes if you prefer a hard cooked egg - or around 5 if you like a more loose yolk - even less if you like a very runny yolk..  Scoop out with a small spoon or dip with toast sticks.  It's a real treat.  These coddlers are very nice because they are clear glass and  go right into the dishwasher. The metal clasps securely hold the lid on which is very important (you don't want water in the coddle) - and are easy to remove with a towel (they will be hot when they come out of the boiling water). The suction is very good and I used it mostly on the low setting, but I don't have pets or children and my floors are laminate or have low pile carpeting so I can't say how it would be on thick carpets, etc. The high power just shortens the battery life. I was happy that the suction was strong enough to pick up crumbs, etc. and didn't just fling bits out the other side. The battery lasted about 30-40 minutes, enough to do my whole apartment with good suction. It takes about 4 hrs to charge the battery, so I wanted to purchase an extra battery to have charged and on hand. It's $33...a third of the vacuum cost...Wow!
